questions.prompt: Why is a Subject both an Observable and an Observer?

options.text: You can subscribe to it, and you can call next/error/complete on it to push values to all subscribers
It converts Promises into Observables automatically
It can only be subscribed to, never emitted to
It runs a fresh producer for each subscriber

questions.explanation: A Subject is subscribable (Observable) and has next/error/complete (Observer). Pushed values multicast to every current subscriber; there is no per-subscriber producer.

questions.prompt: A subscriber joins a plain `Subject` AFTER two values were emitted. What does it receive?

options.text: Nothing from before — only values emitted after it subscribed
Only the most recent earlier value
An error, because it missed values

questions.explanation: A plain Subject has no memory. Late subscribers only see future emissions. Use BehaviorSubject or ReplaySubject to give late subscribers past values.

questions.prompt: Which Subject type requires an initial value and immediately gives new subscribers the current value?
questions.explanation: BehaviorSubject(initial) always holds a current value, replays it on subscribe, and exposes it via .value.

questions.prompt: When does an `AsyncSubject` emit a value to its subscribers?

options.text: Only when it completes — and only its final value
On every next call, like a plain Subject
Immediately on subscribe, using an initial value
It replays the last two values

questions.explanation: AsyncSubject stays silent until complete(), then delivers only the last value to all subscribers — behaving much like a Promise.

questions.prompt: To hand consumers a read-only view of a Subject (so they cannot call next on it), expose `subject.____________`. Type the method call.
questions.explanation: subject.asObservable() returns an Observable that forwards the Subject's emissions but hides next/error/complete, protecting the stream from outside pushes.

questions.prompt: Match each Subject type to what a NEW subscriber receives.

pairs.right: Only values emitted after it subscribes
The current value immediately, then future values
The last two buffered values, then future values
Only the final value, once the subject completes

questions.explanation: Subject has no memory; BehaviorSubject replays the current value; ReplaySubject(n) replays the last n; AsyncSubject emits just the final value on completion.
